question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: Fallen off the radar
solution: The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. Become unnoticed. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"Fallen off the radar"** means to become unnoticed or to no longer be the focus of attention. (ध्यान से हट जाना) • **Example:** After the initial hype, the new product quickly fell off the radar and sales declined. • The correct meaning of this idiom is **"Become unnoticed"**, which implies that something or someone is no longer being tracked, monitored, or given attention. (गौर नहीं किया जा रहा) • **Example:** Many talented artists fall off the radar because they don't get enough opportunities to showcase their work. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2 i.e. Become unnoticed**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Gained attention** (ध्यान आकर्षित किया): To become the center of interest or focus. • **Example:** Her brilliant performance gained a lot of attention from the audience. • **Avoided detection** (पता लगाने से बचना): To successfully escape being noticed or identified. • **Example:** The thief avoided detection by blending into the crowd. • **Gained popularity** (लोकप्रियता प्राप्त करना): To become well-known or liked by a large number of people. • **Example:** The new app quickly gained popularity among young users. 40:Tafb, The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **Taking extreme risks**.
